correctness.rationale: SUB makes all globally IR matchings downward-closed; SUB reduces any set block to a singleton; IRP equates singleton blocking with individually rational one-edge augmentation. Therefore the CY-stable family comprises precisely the facets of the IR complex. SMA accepts exactly feasible extensions, gives a maximal set under any contract order, and attains any prescribed facet by ordering its members first. In the one-firm star, the choice rule C(S)=S on the hereditary hull of the desired antichain and C(S)=empty otherwise satisfies SUB by heredity and IRP by full acceptance upon feasible augmentation. This proves realization of every nonempty antichain, including the empty-set-only case. The finite checker passed all 194 hereditary families on 0..4 elements with 14092 SUB, 3709 IRP, 1440 CY, and 4135 order tests; this is corroboration rather than an infinite proof. An independent complete table enumeration found 67 of the 4096 possible three-contract firm choice functions satisfy SUB and IRP; all 67 also obeyed the stable-facets and SMA order-range equalities.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Existing general existence theorems do not entail the arbitrary-antichain universality claim: an existence result guarantees a single member, while universal antichain realization requires building choices that realize a preassigned entire family. Lattice results under path independence do not dominate the broader SUB-IRP domain. The present statement does not purport to disprove a lattice under every possible order. Bando et al. already consider arbitrary hereditary families, so the feasible-set parametrization is not new by itself. Their priority-prefix choice can fail IRP: for feasible menus {empty,{a},{b}} with a preferred to b, adding a to the IR holding {b} replaces b. The new claim is a SUB-IRP-wide exact stable/facet theorem, every-stable SMA reachability, and an IRP-preserving universal realization; these are stronger/different than the prior priority-prefix feasibility application.

originality.rationale: The closest current source proves an existence algorithm and singleton-block reduction under SUB+IRP, not the exact full order-range theorem nor the realization of every finite antichain. The first version treats a different General Acyclicity model and leaves structural behavior open. The relevant 2025 many-to-one paper defines maximal choice sets and includes three maximal pairs, but it also studies arbitrary hereditary general upper-bounds constraints and greedy priority selection. This is a close feasibility-theoretic antecedent, but its priority-prefix mechanism can violate IRP, and its results do not state the domain-wide CY-stable facet characterization or SMA order-surjectivity of every stable matching. The present IRP choice construction is separate. No equivalent or strictly stronger result was identified in the checked sources and available published summaries; priority risk remains because searches cannot prove absence.

value.rationale: The exact structure of CY-stable matchings under SUB and IRP is an explicitly motivated question in Bansal et al. v9, Section 6. The theorem provides both a positive structural identification (facets of a hereditary IR complex with an order-surjective greedy algorithm) and a tight negative limit on stronger inclusion-shape claims by constructing every nonempty finite antichain on the same simple star architecture. This is a uniform classification and an algorithmic reachability result, rather than a single tiny counterexample or known-table recomputation. The construction is behaviorally unusual but precisely within the axioms being studied.
